# /kav-trailer — the story's preview for other people

A swipeable deck of full-bleed slides, everything in the story's language, nothing that reads like a spec. It sits beside `package/brief.md`: the brief is the page you read, the trailer is the thing you flick through on a phone.

**Register: trailer, not spec.** Every line gestures and withholds. The one-liner never gives away the ending; chapter lines create curiosity, they don't narrate. Reader-facing names are the reader-facing forms. No production details, lanes, packs or internal notes anywhere on it.

## Where it lives

```
stories/<slug>/package/trailer.json     the content (the only thing you edit)
stories/<slug>/package/trailer.html     the built deck
stories/<slug>/package/slides/slide-NN.png   1080×1920 statics (with --statics)
```

## Slide order (adapt per story, keep the arc)

1. **Opener** — the story's key image full-bleed, the title as display type, the one-liner.
2. **Cast divider** — "the characters" in the story language + one breath about who's in it.
3. **One slide per principal character** — round portrait (the styled `front.png`), name, one line.
4. **"And also"** — the rest of the world (background cast, places) on one slide: a generated scene with them in it. Text at the top so the action stays visible.
5. **Contents divider** — a plain table-of-contents slide.
6. **One slide per chapter** — concept image full-bleed, chapter eyebrow, title, the reader-facing synopsis. A drawn chapter shows two pills: **Story** (filled — one panel per screen) and **Comic** (outlined — full pages), linking to its readers; an undrawn chapter shows a quiet "in progress".
7. **Closer** — title · place · "coming soon" or dates.

Content goes into `trailer.json` (see `tools/build_trailer.py --help` and the example in `tools/examples/` for the exact schema): title, opener line, cast entries (name, line, image), the "and also" slide, chapters (title, synopsis, image, reader URLs), closer. Images resolve from the story's own folders only — `cast/<name>/<pack>/front.png`, `storyboard/chNN-concept.png`, `style/samples/`.

## Interaction — like a phone story, not a slideshow

Swipe, or tap a side (left third back, the rest forward). Every line is visible the moment its slide is; nothing types, fills or waits. Arrow keys and space move exactly one slide. On desktop the deck is a centred phone column with arrows outside. Reduced motion: no smooth scroll. No "swipe" hint slide. (The builder implements this; check it when verifying.)

## Building

1. Edit `trailer.json` — the author's lines **verbatim** (fix obvious typos, never rephrase). Swapping an image is a storyboard decision; the author picks.
2. `python3 tools/build_trailer.py --story <slug> --statics` → the deck plus one PNG per slide, rendered from the same page so statics always match the live deck.
3. **Verify.** Look at every `slides/*.png`: text over faces, clipped titles, wrong images. Open `trailer.html` in a browser and actually swipe/tap/arrow through it with real input — synthetic events miss scroll-snap bugs. Phones: check at ≥500px wide renders, since headless Chrome clamps narrower windows.
4. Log the rebuild in `kickoff-state.md` (what changed, why) and record the trailer path under Links.

## Sharing

The deck is a single HTML file plus images; it can go on any static host alongside the chapter readers (`/kav-publish`). The slide PNGs are an Instagram carousel as-is. **Never post or upload anywhere without asking the author.**

## Hard rules

- Reader-facing only. If a line explains instead of previewing, it doesn't go on a slide.
- Story-local images only (the linked style pack is the one exception).
- Statics come from the same build as the live deck — never hand-cropped screenshots.
- Every text change goes through `trailer.json`, then rebuild. The HTML is never edited by hand.
